title: Law & Order: Digital Edition ⚖️
description: Navigate the legal and ethical tightrope every forensic investigator must walk.

slides.title: The Legal Landscape 📜
slides.content:
# Why Law Matters

Digital evidence must be obtained **legally** to be admissible. If you snoop without proper authorization, the evidence gets tossed – and you could face lawsuits or criminal charges.

Key concepts:
- **Search Warrants**: Required unless an exception applies (consent, exigent circumstances).
- **Reasonable Expectation of Privacy**: Does the user have a privacy interest in the data?
- **Jurisdiction**: Data stored in another country may require mutual legal assistance treaties (MLATs).

quizData.question: An employer can always search an employee's work computer without consent.
quizData.explanation: Even on company equipment, employees may retain a reasonable expectation of privacy depending on policies and local laws. Always consult legal counsel.

slides.title: Admissibility: Daubert & Frye ⚖️
slides.content:
Courts use standards to decide if expert evidence (like your forensic analysis) is reliable.

- **Frye Standard**: The methodology must be "generally accepted" in the scientific community.
- **Daubert Standard**: Broader – the judge examines relevance and reliability, considering peer review, error rates, and standards.

> Your tools and techniques must withstand scrutiny!

quizData.question: Which standard requires forensic methods to be 'generally accepted' by the scientific community?
quizData.explanation: The Frye standard focuses on general acceptance, while Daubert gives judges a broader gatekeeper role.

slides.title: Ethics Above All 🤝
slides.content:
## The Ethical Investigator

- **Confidentiality**: Don't discuss case details outside the investigation.
- **Impartiality**: Your loyalty is to the truth, not the person paying you.
- **Competence**: Only accept cases you are qualified to handle.
- **Integrity**: Never tamper with evidence or misrepresent findings.

slides.title: ⚠️ Red Flags
slides.content: Being asked to ignore certain files, skip logging, or work outside your expertise are all ethical red flags. Always document and escalate concerns.

quizData.question: Your manager asks you to 'just take a quick look' at a personal phone without a warrant to speed up an internal investigation. What should you do?

options.text: Proceed because it's a company matter
Refuse and explain the legal and ethical implications
Ask a colleague to do it instead

quizData.explanation: An ethical investigator must uphold the law and professional standards, even if pressured. Refusing and educating is the right path.

slides.title: When in Doubt 🚀
slides.content:
## Consult Legal Counsel

Never guess about legality. The best forensicators build strong relationships with their organization's legal team.
